The Stephen McGown story.

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In his first in- depth television interview , Stephen McGown speaks about his six year ordeal while being held by al-Qaeda.

Unique Selling Point:
Stephen McGown was kidnapped at a hotel in the historic trading city of Timbuktu in Mali's north along with Swede Johan Gustafsson and Dutchman Sjaak Rijke, both of whom have subsequently been released. What was intended to be an adventure motorbike ride across Africa turned into a five and a half year ordeal at the hands of al-Oaeda.


Summary:
Stephen often feared for his life and at times was held in handcuffs and chains at night. With only one blanket Stephen and fellow hostages had to build a structure from leaves to keep out the freezing desert evening cold. After converting to Islam, he received better treatment from his captors, receiving better clothing and food. He entered Islam of his own accord. He sees many good things in Islam. It requires a good and strict character. Stephen tried to develop coping techniques. Sometimes sleeping, exercising,, trying to see the best in the situation and never giving up hope on returning to his family.
It was an extremely difficult time for his parents Malcolm and Beverley. Malcolm offered to trade places with his son. Although elated at his son's release, there was also great sadness as Beverley passed away in May this year,two months before Stephen's release.

Press Release:


Stephen McGown
It was supposed to be the adventure of a lifetime – the ultimate motorcycle ride across Africa. Instead, it
turned into almost 6 years of hell at the hands of al-Qaeda. Kidnapped, chained and constantly fearing for
his life, Stephen McGown clung to the hope of being reunited with his family and was finally released in
August. In his first in-depth television interview, he opens up to Carte Blanche about his terrifying ordeal.

Script:


The Stephen McGown Story
V/o
UPSOUND:

Hostage video I emplore the SA government to negotiate for my release and return me home soon. Please help me, please give me my freedom... please return me back to my family...
VO from old story – this edited paragraph is from the old story.
Almost six years ago, Stephen McGown embarked on a motorbike ride from the top of Africa to Johannesburg where he was supposed to meet up with his wife Cath. But when he got to Timbuktu in Mali, things went horribly wrong.
Devi Link On the 25th of November 2011 South African Stephen McGown and two others were captured in Mali by al Qaeda.
Stephen McGown
Up sound It just happened so quickly> It went from a beautiful day – blue skies, sitting on the patio of this hotel and next thing guys walk in with a gun.
V/o
Show picture of that vehicle in an empty street here… On a dusty road, Swedish National Johan Gustafson and Dutchman Sjaak Rikje, were loaded onto the vehicle with Stephen on that fateful day.
Stephen
up-sound They were beating me with my shoe, my shoe had come off, they beat me with my shoe. One of the other hostages, he was beaten with a belt, just to sort of hurry us up to get us to the car!
Devi
V/O

It was Stephen’s life long dream to travel through Africa on his motorbike. Even though she had concerns about his safety, his wife of four years, Cath, gave him five months to fulfil his dream, before starting a family..
Devi
V/O Then early on the Saturday morning the phone rang in the McGown house in Johannesburg.
Malcolm McGown I picked it up and it was the person he was riding with, Volker van den Berg's mother from Holland and she introduced herself and I said don't tell me something's gone wrong and she said have you heard from Stephen and I said no. And she said well I'm afraid he's been taken by Al-Queda.
Stephen I'm thinking what am I going to say to my family? I've been allowed 5 months by my wife. This cannot be happening. It didn't seem real.
V/o The three hostages, later know as the Timbuktu three, spent 15 hours driving through the Sahara concealed under cargo nets.

Stephen It was a wild trip. We were just literally on the metal work. So we were bouncing on the metal work. I had a cut above my left eye here from banging up against the wheel arch.
Devi So at the beginning, where were you held?
Stephen
Up-sound It was basically a six year camping trip if you like. We started off in the mountains, then we moved from the mountains across to the desert and then we moved down into Timbuktu for a month, So of my 5 years 8 months it was one month in prison, if you like, in Timbuktu and then 5 years 7 months in the Sahara.
V/o Stephen was traveling on his British passport and soon realized that this might have sealed his fate.
Stephen
Up-sound Things became particularly weird within the camps. These guys would have their radios on and there would be a lot of Brittania, Brittania, Brittania... I mean there was one experience, just before they took there was a meeting going on with all the senior Al-Qaeda guys and there was a little kid – 8 or 9 year old sitting amongst them. They'd look at me, they're talking Brittania and they talking about me. And then the 8 year old walked away from the circle with a packet of crisps. Sitting there eating crisps. Starts looking for me. I look up, we catch eyes. He looks at me and does this. You, and he sits and he eats his chips. That day I thought I was dead.
Stephen



When all these things got strange, I was like If I'm going to die let me just do this now, so I converted.
V/O After much soul searching, Stephen converted to Islam.
It does save your life, if you like. When you become Muslim there are certain rules within Islam which protects Muslims.
Devi
Were they kinder to you?
Stephen Things changed dramatically. All of a sudden we weren't chained at night, we weren't blindfolded on journeys. There was no more death threats from the 8-year old or anybody else.
Devi
v/o The hostages were moved around constantly, by the heavily armed Muja/hadien, spending hours out in the searing desert heat.
Stephen The first couple of months in the Sahara were exceptionally difficult just trying to fill your day. You've got nothing. You've got sand, you've got rocks. You've got a couple a couple of trees. You've got nothing.
Devi What were you given to eat?
Stephen We ate a lot of spagetti and rice.
Stephen We would bring in goats and sheep and occasionally a camel. And we would then slaughter this and skin it and prepare the meat and hang the meat up to dry. Some of those situations were quite unusual. I mean... In summer you store the meat for 2 days and the meat goes off. In winter you can store it probably for a week and then it starts to get a smell and go off. But I don't know how many times we had worms in our food . There were worms in the meat and they get boiled up in the food, so we weren't sure if it was rice or worms....
V/o Halfway through their ordeal, Swedish hostage Johan Gustaffson managed to escape.
Stephen We did speak about running away and the possibilities, but to me it seemed slightly crazy, you know. Is it better to run away and die or is it better to run away and come back and maybe have your feet cut off – we're not sure what will happen. And for me I don't particularly want to die.
V/o Gustafson was recaptured the very next day and brought back.
Stephen After this our situation became incredibly difficult. We weren't able to do exercise. All our things were confiscated. We couldn’t leave the hut. Things were taken from us at night.
V/o
O/lay Hostage video

Back home, Stephen’s parents, Malcolm and Beverley received another video from his captors – proof that he was still alive.
Old story:
Strap Carte Blanche January 2014 Bev McGown: I noticed that they put clean clothes on him … it was a relief to see that he was still alive.
LINK It was only in Dec 2015 Dr Sooliman, head of Gift of the Givers, was sent this proof of life video.
VIDEO My name is Stephen McGown. I'm a South African citizen. Today’s date is the 20th of October 2015....
Devi What happened after that?
Stephen Well nothing, if you like from our point of view. I was given this hope that you should be going home soon, there's this Muslim organisation trying to help you....

V/O Two years later he was eventually released.
Devi When did you hear that your release was eminent?
Stephen A guy just sort of said... go. I'm like what? He said yeh you can go.
V/o Once again Stephen was loaded onto a vehicle and driven through the desert and eventually onto a tar road.

Stephen You forget what a road looks like and when I saw this my heart was beating such a hole in my chest> I was like, hang on a second pal, just settle down. Don't think you're going home because they're just putting you somewhere else for the moment.
V/o They drove for a couple of days, sleeping on the side of the road and dodging road blocks until they reached the capital city Bamako.
Stephen I went to the airport the following day and there was a plane waiting for me
V/o Early on the Sunday morning Stephen arrived in SA and was driven to his family home by government officials. But it was just before arrival that he was informed that sadly his mother has passed away two months prior to his release.
Stephen I arrived back and my dad and I didn't speak about my mom's passing away that day – we did not speak about it. It did not seem the right thing to speak about on my arrival home.
Stephen I think the following day we spoke about it and we went up to the Kruger park and scattered some ashes in the Kruger and my dad turned across to me... I was driving, my dad was next to me in the front seat. And he turned and looked at me and put his hand on my shoulder and he said to me you know you had a beautiful mother. And ja... That was me anyway. That was tickets. After that I was hiding behind my dark glasses. I was probably in tears for a half a day after that.
V/O Throughout his ordeal Stephen always put his family first.
Stephen From my side I wanted to come home and have my wife and have my mom here, you know and I was assuming it would not take 5 months not 5 years 8 months. But after 4 years I was like, well I want what's best for my wife, what is best for her and if I come home and I don’t have a wife then I come home and I don't have a wife but I want what is best for my wife. but I came home and my wife is here and our marriage is better than it was.
Devi So what does the future hold for you?
Stephen

Well, I'm excited. I think it going to be only good times, I hope. Change of career. I was doing something which did not speak to me, it was not my kind of thing, so now I wanna do things I enjoy and I wanna hang out with my mates and my family and have quality time and good conversations and not allow life to take hold of me really. Be in control of life if you like....

PROMO 10” In an in-depth interview we speak to Stephen McGown, who spent almost six years of his life in the Sahara desert at the mercy of the terrorists who captured him in 2011.

PROMO 15” What was life like as a hostage in the Sahara desert?

UPSOUND
The first couple of months in the Sahara were exceptionally difficult just trying to fill your day. You've got nothing. You've got sand, you've got rocks. You've got a couple a couple of trees. You've got nothing.

Stephen McGown tells his story....


PROMO 15” For 5 years and 8 months Stephen McGown lived as a hostage at the hands of the al-Qaeda Muja/hadien.

UPSOUND
I'm not going to run away into bandit territory, into places where we don't know where the wells are. I mean where? Run into where?
